newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei end weak as poor sentiment persists.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei end weak as poor sentiment persists.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures slipped back below the 18,000-points level by Thursday's close, as players saw little reason to extend the previous day's gains amid continuing weak sentiment.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract lost 90 points to end at 17,950 after hitting a high of 18,160. Volume was relatively light at 14,715 lots.

Nikkei cash and futures markets made strong gains on Wednesday on media reports senior members of Japan's Liberal Democratic Party were calling for the scrapping of taxes on securities transactions to help boost stock prices.

But a Japanese finance ministry official told Reuters on Thursday that such a measure would be considered as part of an overall reform of Japan's tax system and not a specific measure to deal with recent weakness in the Tokyo stock market.
"People realised that the tax package talk was just a lot of hot air. Until they come out with something specific, the market is just going to sit here for a few days and then dump," said a trader.
He said the March Nikkei could consolidate around 18,000 for the next few days, but would then be vulnerable to a steep decline in the absence of any concrete measures.

"The market will only denounce its downtrend and enter a consolidation if it can take out 18,750. That would indicate that the bottom is in place, but it'll be tough," said a trader with a local futures house.
He said continued weakness in the yen could cause foreign funds to unload Japanese stocks.
MSCI Taiwan index futures had their most active session since the contract's launch on January 9, with an estimated turnover of 876 lots in the March contract.
It ended 3.3 points down at 310.5 after hitting a high of 322.0 in early trade.
Dealers said there was increased participation by securities houses and retail investors, and some even detected the presence of Taiwanese players.
"The ranges are getting larger and we're starting to see more institutions represented in the pit," said a trader.
The Taiwan stock market opened sharply up on hopes an unofficial Taiwan-China consensus reached Wednesday could end a decades-old ban on direct shipping links between the two areas.
But profit-taking eroded the gains, causing the index to reverse course and close 71.22 points down at 7,219.55 after hitting a high of 7,391.94. -- Sonali Desai (65-8703090)
